title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text: Live in production · runs daily

title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text:
The problem
Weekly submission statistics depended on a legacy Excel VBA macro that downloaded one email per second, ran once a week, and locked the computer while it worked. Parsing email titles into fields produced wrong and missing values, so every run was followed by manual edits. The volume: around 500 submissions per week, on top of an archive of roughly 120,000 emails.

  BeforeOne email per second. Weekly runs that froze the machine. Wrong parsing, manual corrections every week, statistics in a fragile Excel file.
  AfterA background Python script feeding a clean CSV archive since 2019, with a live Power BI dashboard on top. No pivot tables, no manual refresh.

title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text:
What I built
A Python application with a small GUI: you pick the Outlook folder, pick the mode, and run. The parser normalises dates and applies 57 regex patterns to extract the right fields from inconsistent email titles. Output is a clean CSV rather than Excel, which handles the 120,000-email archive without strain. That CSV feeds a Power BI semantic model connected through SharePoint, with dynamic graphs that automatically adapt to the latest weeks in the dataset. All documentation lives in QMD files rendered to HTML.



Pipeline overview


The script can run automatically on computer start or manually for double checks, so the data is daily by default instead of weekly by ritual.

title: Email Pipeline & Submission Dashboard
text:
Outcome
Around 5 hours saved every week, plus the manual checks and corrections that no longer exist. The team now has consistent, clean data since 2019 and a dashboard that is always current.



GUI and dashboard


Stack: Python (GUI, regex parsing), CSV, SharePoint, Power BI semantic model, Quarto documentation

title: Live Revenue & Expenditure Dashboard
text: Live in production · Expenditure model in development

title: Live Revenue & Expenditure Dashboard
text:
The problem
Revenue and expenditure reporting at the organisation depended on more than 20 separate SAP reports, each extracted by hand as an Excel file. Filters were applied inside individual workbooks and could not be traced afterwards. Data structures differed between teams, so Finance, Procurement and others routinely produced numbers that disagreed with each other.

  Before20+ manual Excel extracts. Untraceable filters. Monthly or quarterly refresh, on a different schedule per team. Hundreds of inconsistencies between reports.
  AfterOne governed pipeline. Filters and fields defined once, at the source. Daily refresh at enterprise level. Around 10 fact tables, clean data back to 2020.

title: Live Revenue & Expenditure Dashboard
text:
What I built
I helped rewrite most of the data ingestion around one idea: a live connection instead of file exports. Working with SAP consultants, we moved the source layer to SAP Datasphere and rebuilt the data model there, so every filter and field lives in one place instead of inside someone’s workbook. A live gateway then feeds the Power BI dashboard directly, currently around 10 fact tables for the Revenue model with clean data since 2020. The Expenditure side is in development on the same foundation.



End to end data flow


The trade off: building the model centrally was slower upfront than fixing individual reports, and it required cross-team agreement on definitions. That agreement is exactly what removed the inconsistencies.

title: Live Revenue & Expenditure Dashboard
text:
Outcome
Refresh frequency went from monthly or quarterly (and different per team) to daily for the whole organisation. The change saved around 40 collective working hours per week across the teams involved in reporting, and resolved more than 300 inconsistencies between reporting mechanisms and incorrect values.



Data model view


Stack: SAP Datasphere, SQL, Power BI (live gateway), Python, Databricks

title: About
text:
Open to interesting problems
I am a finance data engineer. My background is finance and portfolio management (MSc, University of Rome Tor Vergata), and my day to day is making financial data flow without human glue: SQL pipelines, Python tooling, Power BI, and lately agentic AI systems that I keep on a short leash. I currently work in financial management for a European Union agency in Amsterdam.

title: About
text:
How I work

  01Map first, build secondEvery tool I ship started as an Excel file someone updated by hand. I map the manual steps first, then automate only where it pays for itself.
  02Boring interfaces winThe best tool is the one the team actually uses. Drop files in a folder, click run. If adoption needs a manual, the design failed.
  03Document or it does not existA tool nobody else can run is a liability. Everything I build ships with rendered documentation and a guide, so it survives me being on holiday.

title: Invoice Reconciliation Tool
text: Live in production · team adopted

title: Invoice Reconciliation Tool
text:
The problem
Checking supplier invoices meant combining 5 separate SAP extracts against a reference table in a static shared database, where each person uploaded and downloaded the latest version. Across several teams this turned into chaos: constant reminders, emails back and forth, and no certainty about which file was current. Each cycle covered more than 200 invoices and disputes, some open for years, across many procedure types.

  BeforeManual merge of 5 extracts. Upload and download of a shared file. Reminder emails. Checks that were sometimes wrong and always slow.
  AfterDrop the new reports in a folder, run the tool, get a verified master file with a colour coded summary. Instant, logged, archived.

title: Invoice Reconciliation Tool
text:
What I built
A fully automated script packaged as a standalone EXE, so the team runs it without installing Python. The workflow: drop the new SAP reports into the downloads folder, run the tool. It validates the file formats, extracts the data, applies all matching, transformation, checking and deduplication rules, archives the input files with timestamps, writes a run log, and produces a master CSV holding the full archive. On top of that sits an Excel view with colour coded checks and an embedded summary table, because the people reading it live in Excel.



Reconciliation flow


The trade off: shipping an EXE means I own packaging and updates. In exchange, adoption was immediate, since nobody had to learn a new tool beyond “drop files, click run”.

title: Invoice Reconciliation Tool
text:
Outcome
A single source of truth where there used to be five files and an argument. Around 10 hours of weekly work saved, plus the removal of manual checks that regularly produced wrong results. The script processes all extracts simultaneously and writes thousands of rows to the master file in seconds.



GUI and Excel summary


Stack: Python (packaged EXE), pandas-style data matching, CSV master file, Excel reporting layer

title: Living Documentation System
text: Live · in daily team use

title: Living Documentation System
text:
The problem
Team documentation lived in Word files full of screenshots and links that broke over time. Versions diverged across teams, changes were untracked, and every update meant manual fixes throughout the document.

  BeforeWord documents, broken links, manual screenshot updates, no way to track which version was current.
  AfterOne QMD template and one stylesheet. Every document renders to HTML in an identical, current, linkable format.

title: Living Documentation System
text:
What I built
A documentation system for the team based on Quarto: a QMD document template, a reporting template, and a shared style.css carrying the house colours, so every output looks the same regardless of who wrote it. Documents render to HTML with a dynamic table of contents, collapsable sections, cross references to each other, and images and graphs that update with the underlying data instead of being pasted in.



System overview


This is also the quiet enabler of the other projects on this site: every tool I ship comes with documentation in this format, so it survives me being on holiday.

title: Living Documentation System
text:
Outcome
Interconnected, linkable documents that can be reproduced in the same format every time. Managers get consistent reporting; the team gets documentation that is actually current. Video guides complement the written docs for onboarding.



Documentation examples


Stack: Quarto (QMD), HTML, CSS, video editing for guides
